clue.text: Superb surroundings for vineyard arise because of natural growth

indicators.note: the first word is presented as forming the surroundings, wrapping around the next one

parts.note: ace means excellent, first-rate
a cru is a French vineyard or its wine

explanation.surface: A wine lover praises a superb setting for a vineyard that has grown up naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: A cru is a French term for a classed vineyard or its wine, a word met mostly on wine labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest or benefits that accrue build up gradually as an organic increase over time.

clue.text: This humiliation makes Jill (not Jack) ill

parts.words: This humiliation makes Jill (not Jack) ill
parts.note: surface reading: a nursery-rhyme girl is left sick and embarrassed
setter's reading: take the J, the jack being a face card and the first letter the face of the word, off Jill and ill remains

explanation.surface: Jill of the nursery rhyme, left without Jack, is sickened by her embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing J from JILL leaves ILL; J is the Jack, a face card in playing cards, and also the word's front, so the operation is a LOSS OF FACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing face is the idiom for suffering public embarrassment and a drop in standing or dignity.

clue.text: Pervert said lust reduced conflict

indicators.note: to pervert is to twist out of shape, so the following word's letters get twisted

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter of the word before is dropped

parts.note: greed is excessive desire, a synonym for lust

explanation.surface: Someone claims that curbed desire led to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: SAID is rearranged to DISA, and GREED loses its last letter to give GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to conflict and to disagree both mean to be at odds or hold opposing views.

clue.text: Having turned corner, lose front end and cause injury

indicators.note: losing the front end means the first letter of the word for corner is removed

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off
a bend in the road is a corner

explanation.surface: A driver takes a corner, loses the front of the car, and someone gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: BEND drops its B to give END.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense, to offend is to harm or wound, besides the usual meaning of hurting feelings.

clue.text: One making a contribution to community

indicators.note: the answer contributes some of the letters inside the following word, sitting within it

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Someone plays their part in a local neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing or the number one, the basic quantity used in counting.

clue.text: Mature children embracing adult with child

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the first part wraps around the rest

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A family scene: the kids hug a grown-up holding a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed meaning descendants is a biblical usage, as in 'the seed of Abraham'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned and mature both describe someone experienced, or food and wood that has aged properly.

clue.text: Tweet about profit-sharing enterprise bailing out?

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the enterprise

parts.note: birds tweet, that is sing
a co-op shares its profits among its members

explanation.surface: A social-media post about a cooperative business being rescued financially.
explanation.walkthrough: Bailing out is meant to suggest a financial rescue, but it is scooping water out of a boat; the question mark flags that it is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bailing water out of a boat is done by scooping it up with a bucket or container.

clue.text: Achieve recognition with wins over United and Premier League club

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the word for wins is placed around united

parts.note: to win is to gain
united people are as one
Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: A football side earns acclaim by beating Manchester United and Tottenham.
explanation.walkthrough: United looks like Manchester United, another club, but it simply means joined together as one.
explanation.definitionFit: To win one's spurs, like a medieval knight, is an idiom for first proving oneself and earning distinction.

clue.text: Redhead takes a step back at first touch

indicators.text: takes a step back at first
indicators.note: the opening letter moves back one place in the alphabet, a single step backwards

parts.note: ginger is a British nickname for someone with red hair

explanation.surface: A red-haired person retreats a pace the moment they are touched.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of GINGER steps back one letter in the alphabet to F, giving FINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger something is to feel or handle it with the fingers, so to touch it.

clue.text: Dismiss sweeper for each team

parts.note: a brush sweeps
a means per, as in 'five pounds a head'
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A football manager drops the sweeper position from every team sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweeper is also a defensive position in football, which is the picture the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush aside an objection is to dismiss it curtly without considering it properly.

clue.text: Job centre in Stockport was located on turning

indicators.note: turning round means the combined letters are read from right to left
the centre of the town name is its single middle letter

parts.note: Stockport is a town near Manchester; its fifth of nine letters
something located somewhere sat there

explanation.surface: A jobcentre was found on a bend in the road in Stockport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job centre' reads as one phrase, the British unemployment office, but 'Job' is the definition and 'centre' selects a letter. K and SAT together turned round give TASK.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, so a job in the sense of a chore.

clue.text: Successor accepting reduced charge is a little lower

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for successor holds the other part

parts.note: an heir succeeds to a title or estate

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word for charge loses its tail letter

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: An heir agreeing to a cut fee ends up slightly lower down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'further down' but 'one who lows', that is moos, so a little lower is a young cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow, and cattle low, so it is a small mooing animal.

clue.text: Blonde man dyes locks whenever required

indicators.note: locks means holds fast inside, so the phrase keeps the answer enclosed within it

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A fair-haired man colours his hair whenever he needs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests hair, fitting the dye picture, but it is the signal that the answer is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: On demand means as soon as or whenever asked for, as with a streaming service.

clue.text: Recent mail shot in connection with trade

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or ruined, so the letters before it are broken up

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A recent mailshot, a bulk advertising letter, was sent out to businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile describes merchants and commerce, so concerned with buying and selling goods.

clue.text: Fantastic war novel we borrowed on vacation about resistance work

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and unreal, so the letters are wildly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: vacating a word empties it, leaving just its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A war novel that we borrowed is a fantastic piece of writing about the Resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War novel' suggests the genre, but the words are just fodder. The answer is Aldous Huxley's 1932 dystopian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave New World is a celebrated novel by Aldous Huxley, so a literary work.

clue.text: Make allowances for beast like Rupert Murdoch finally being the butt of humour

parts.note: Rupert Bear is a British children's comic-strip character
wit is cleverness in humour

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of the surname is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: The media tycoon Rupert Murdoch, as a brute, becomes a target of jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Murdoch seems one person, but the first name points to Rupert Bear. 'Being the butt of' puts the H at the end, the butt, of WIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear with me is the idiom for asking someone to be patient and tolerant for a moment.

clue.text: Saw flute ad-lib, blowing too many notes?

indicators.note: to ad-lib is to improvise freely, so the letters are played in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flautist improvises and plays far more notes than the tune needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Blowing notes looks musical, but it means squandering banknotes; the question mark marks the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing banknotes means spending money freely, and doing too much of that is extravagant and squandering.

clue.text: Openings of English country dances transposed chord changes

indicators.note: transposed means moved into a different order, as music is moved to another key
the openings of words are their first letters

parts.note: the initial letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: The opening tunes of English country dances are shifted to new keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English country dances' reads as one folk-dance phrase, but only the first two words give initials.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a cadence is a sequence of chords closing a phrase, so a series of harmonic shifts.

clue.text: Rounded channel turning axis through 90 degrees

indicators.note: on a graph a quarter turn swaps one axis for the other, so one axis letter replaces the other

parts.note: to channel something is to convey or transmit it

explanation.surface: A geometry problem: a channel is rotated a quarter-turn about its axis.
explanation.walkthrough: Graph axes are labelled x and y and are at right angles, so swapping the Y of CONVEY for X gives CONVEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Convex describes a surface that curves outwards like the outside of a sphere.

clue.text: Short break at empty property

parts.note: to snap is to break suddenly

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving the outside letters only

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A brief holiday spent at a vacant house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short break' looks like a mini-holiday, but 'Short' is the definition and 'break' the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A snappy reply is curt and abrupt, and snappy writing is brief and crisp.

clue.text: Criticise railway about entrance to terminal where one obtains fare

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first two pieces sit around the selected letter

parts.note: critics pan a poor show

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A passenger complains about the railway near the station where tickets are bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price at a railway terminal; here it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a larder or store cupboard for food, and fare means food and drink.

clue.text: Cotton on sticky part of plant?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grasp or realise, informal British
second meaning: a small stick growing from a branch

explanation.surface: Cotton fibre clinging to a gummy bit of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticky' suggests gluey, but it means like a stick; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is British slang for suddenly understanding, and a twig is a thin stick-like shoot of a tree.

clue.text: Spiritual guide misinterpreted augury's contents

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so the letters come out in a different order
the contents of a word are the letters inside it, without its ends

parts.note: the inner letters of augury

explanation.surface: A mystic teacher reads an omen wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a Hindu spiritual teacher, and more widely a respected mentor.

clue.text: Offensive article about University Chairs

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the article is written backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
U is the standard abbreviation for university
chairs collectively are seating

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece attacking university professors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairs' suggests professors holding chairs at a university, but it is just furniture to sit on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauseating means sickening or disgusting, so deeply objectionable to the senses or sensibilities.

clue.text: Fast introduction to rondo separates part of score

indicators.note: the letter splits the part of score into two halves by sitting between them

parts.note: a stave is the set of five lines music is written on

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A quick rondo opening splits up a section of the musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like a tempo marking in this musical picture, but it means go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food, and to starve is to suffer from lack of it.

clue.text: One has a row by rear of utility room next to kitchen

parts.note: a sculler rows a boat

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone argues beside the utility room, which adjoins the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument, but it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery is a small back room off a kitchen used for washing dishes and rough chores.
